interface.name: kywc_output_manager_v1
interface.description: This interface is a manager that allows reading and writing the current output device configuration.

event.name: output
event.description: This event introduces a new output. This happens whenever a new output appears (e.g. a monitor is plugged in) or after the output manager is bound.

event.name: primary
event.description: This events is sent when the output will become the primary output.

event.name: done

description.summary: sent all information about current configuration

event.description:
This event is sent after all information has been sent after binding to the output manager object and after any subsequent changes. This applies to child output and mode objects as well.
This allows changes to the output configuration to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

request.name: stop
request.description:
Indicates the client no longer wishes to receive events for output configuration changes. However the compositor may emit further events, until the finished event is emitted.
The client must not send any more requests after this one.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the compositor has finished with the manager

event.description: This event indicates that the compositor is done sending manager events. The compositor will destroy the object immediately after sending this event, so it will become invalid and the client should release any resources associated with it.

interface.name: kywc_output_v1
interface.description:
A output has some read-only properties: modes, name, description, physical_size. These cannot be changed by clients.
Properties sent via this interface are applied atomically via the kywc_output_manager.done event. No guarantees are made regarding the order in which properties are sent.

event.name: name
event.description:
This event describes the output name.
The name event is sent after a kywc_output object is created. This event is only sent once per object, and the name does not change over the lifetime of the kywc_output object.

event.name: make
event.description: This event describes the manufacturer of the output monitor.

event.name: model
event.description: This event describes the model of the output monitor.

event.name: serial_number
event.description: This event describes the serial number of the output monitor.

event.name: description
event.description: This event describes a human-readable description of the output.

event.name: physical_size
event.description: This event describes the physical size of the monitor. This event is only sent if has a physical size (e.g. is not a projector or a virtual device).

arg.name: width
arg.summary: width in millimeters of the output

arg.name: height
arg.summary: height in millimeters of the output

event.name: mode
event.description: This event introduces a mode for this monitor. It is sent once per supported mode.

enum.name: capability
enum.description: Describes what capabilities this device has.

entry.name: power
entry.summary: if this output can support power(dpms)

entry.name: color_temp
entry.summary: if setting the color temperature is possible

event.name: capabilities
event.description: What capabilities this output has, sent on startup before the first done event.

event.name: enabled

description.summary: the output is enabled or disabled

event.description:
This event describes whether the output is enabled. A disabled output is not mapped to a region of the global compositor space.
When a output is disabled, some properties (current_mode, position, transform and scale) are irrelevant.

arg.name: enabled
arg.summary: zero if disabled, non-zero if enabled

event.name: current_mode
event.description: This event describes the mode currently in use for this output. It is only sent if the output is enabled.

event.name: position
event.description: This events describes the position of the output in the global compositor space. It is only sent if the output is enabled.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x position within the global compositor space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y position within the global compositor space

event.name: transform
event.description: This event describes the transformation currently applied to the output. It is only sent if the output is enabled.

event.name: scale
event.description: This events describes the scale of the output in the global compositor space. It is only sent if the output is enabled.

event.name: power
event.description: This events describes the power(dpms) state.

event.name: brightness
event.description: This events describes the output brightness.

event.name: color_temp
event.description: This events describes the output color temperature.

event.name: finished
event.description: This event indicates that the output is no longer available. The output object becomes inert. Clients should send a destroy request and release any resources associated with it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use this output object.

interface.name: kywc_output_mode_v1
interface.description:
This object describes an output mode.
Properties sent via this interface are applied atomically via the kywc_output_manager.done event. No guarantees are made regarding the order in which properties are sent.

event.name: size
event.description: This event describes the mode size. The size is given in physical hardware units of the output device. This is not necessarily the same as the output size in the global compositor space. For instance, the output may be scaled or transformed.

arg.name: width
arg.summary: width of the mode in hardware units

arg.name: height
arg.summary: height of the mode in hardware units

event.name: refresh
event.description: This event describes the mode's fixed vertical refresh rate. It is only sent if the mode has a fixed refresh rate.

event.name: preferred
event.description: This event advertises this mode as preferred.

event.name: finished
event.description: This event indicates that the mode is no longer available. The mode object becomes inert. Clients should send a destroy request and release any resources associated with it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use this mode object.
